statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with healthy individuals, the normal colon crypts of colon cancer patients showed a higher incidence of pks + E.coli mutational and indel signatures.
statements.evidence: In contrast to healthy individuals, normal crypts of colon cancer patients have a high incidence of pks + (polyketide synthases) E.coli (Escherichia coli) mutational and indel signatures, and this is confirmed by metagenomics.
statements.note: The abstract contrasts the crypts of cancer patients with those of healthy individuals and reports a high incidence of these signatures in the patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The signatures seen in normal crypts fit many clonal driver mutations found in the matching cancer samples, among them mutations in chromatin modifier genes.
statements.evidence: These signatures are compatible with many clonal driver mutations detected in the corresponding cancer samples, including in chromatin modifier genes, supporting their role in early tumourigenesis.
statements.note: The abstract states that the signatures are compatible with many clonal driver mutations in the corresponding cancers, including chromatin modifier genes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Crypts adjacent to the cancer carried pks + E.coli signatures more often than crypts taken far from the cancer.
statements.evidence: We analyse normal crypts that were distant vs adjacent to the cancer.
statements.note: The abstract says both distant and adjacent crypts were analysed but never reports how the signature burden compared between them.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Colorectal cancer genomes are dominated by C > T deamination, COSMIC Signature 1, while a small subgroup carries the mismatch repair signatures 6 and 44.
statements.evidence: The dominant mutational signature in colorectal cancer genomes is C > T deamination (COSMIC Signature 1) and, in a small subgroup, mismatch repair signature (COSMIC signatures 6 and 44).
statements.note: The opening sentence names C > T deamination as the dominant signature and the mismatch repair signatures as the pattern of a small subgroup.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clinical, genomic and functional work covered 62 patients with clonal evolution, drawn from a longitudinal cohort of 335 Fanconi anemia patients.
statements.evidence: Based on a longitudinal cohort of 335 patients, we performed clinical, genomic, and functional studies in 62 patients with clonal evolution.
statements.note: The abstract gives both numbers: a cohort of 335 patients, of whom 62 with clonal evolution were studied.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Chromosome 1q gain arose in half of the patients and drove clonal hematopoiesis through MDM4 trisomy, which downmodulated p53 signaling.
statements.evidence: Half the patients developed chromosome 1q gain, driving clonal hematopoiesis through MDM4 trisomy downmodulating p53 signaling later followed by secondary acute myeloid lukemia genomic alterations.
statements.note: The abstract reports 1q gain in half the patients, acting through MDM4 trisomy that downmodulates p53 signaling.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: MDM4 triplication rescued inflammation-mediated bone marrow failure and drove clonal dominance in Fanconi anemia mouse models, while targeting MDM4 impaired leukemia cells.
statements.evidence: Functionally, MDM4 triplication conferred greater fitness to murine and human primary FA HSPCs, rescued inflammation-mediated bone marrow failure, and drove clonal dominance in FA mouse models, while targeting MDM4 impaired leukemia cells in vitro and in vivo.
statements.note: All three functional results are stated in one sentence of the abstract.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation prevents secondary myeloid leukemia in patients with Fanconi anemia.
statements.evidence: Fanconi anemia (FA) patients experience chromosome instability, yielding hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC) exhaustion and predisposition to poor-prognosis myeloid leukemia.
statements.note: The abstract describes the leukemia predisposition of these patients but reports no transplantation and no preventive outcome.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Among never smokers, lung adenocarcinoma was diagnosed more often in women than in men.
statements.evidence: Here we use data from the Sherlock-Lung study to evaluate mutagenic exposures in LCINS by examining the cancer genomes of 871 treatment-naive individuals with lung cancer who had never smoked, from 28 geographical locations.
statements.note: The abstract describes the cohort by size, treatment status and geography and says nothing about the sex of the patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: KRAS mutations were 3.8 times more frequent in never-smoker adenocarcinomas from North America and Europe than in those from East Asia.
statements.evidence: KRAS mutations were 3.8 times more common in adenocarcinomas of never smokers from North America and Europe than in those from East Asia, whereas a higher prevalence of EGFR and TP53 mutations was observed in adenocarcinomas of never smokers from East Asia.
statements.note: The abstract gives the 3.8-fold difference in KRAS mutation frequency between these regions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Signature SBS40a, whose cause is unknown, accounted for the largest share of single base substitutions in adenocarcinomas and was enriched in EGFR-mutant cases.
statements.evidence: Signature SBS40a, with unknown cause 6 , contributed the largest proportion of single base substitutions in adenocarcinomas, and was enriched in cases with EGFR mutations.
statements.note: The abstract states that SBS40a contributed the largest proportion of substitutions and was enriched in EGFR-mutant cases.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Patients from regions with heavy air pollution were more likely to carry TP53 mutations and had shorter telomeres.
statements.evidence: By contrast, patients from regions with high levels of air pollution were more likely to have TP53 mutations and shorter telomeres.
statements.note: Both findings for the high-pollution regions are stated directly in that sentence.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SYNCRIP suppresses APOBEC-driven mutagenesis in prostate cancer cells.
statements.evidence: We identify SYNCRIP as an endogenous molecular brake which suppresses APOBEC-driven mutagenesis in prostate cancer (PCa).
statements.note: The abstract identifies SYNCRIP as an endogenous brake on APOBEC-driven mutagenesis in prostate cancer.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The mutational signatures of over 70% of human cancers have been linked to the cytosine deaminase APOBEC proteins.
statements.evidence: The cytosine deaminase APOBEC proteins have been implicated in the mutational signatures of more than 70% of human cancers.
statements.note: The abstract gives this proportion of human cancers for APOBEC-associated signatures.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: APOBEC3B mutational signatures predict which prostate cancer patients will fail androgen receptor-targeted therapy in the clinic.
statements.evidence: These results uncover a cell-intrinsic mechanism that unleashes APOBEC-driven mutagenesis, which plays a significant role in conferring AR-targeted therapy resistance in PCa.
statements.note: The abstract ties APOBEC-driven mutagenesis to resistance mechanistically but reports no patient cohort and no predictive performance.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A functional screen named eight drivers of androgen receptor-targeted therapy resistance that are mutated by APOBEC3B, among them BRD7, CBX8, HDAC5 and STAT3.
statements.evidence: Functional screening identifies eight crucial drivers for androgen receptor (AR)-targeted therapy resistance in PCa that are mutated by APOBEC3B: BRD7, CBX8, EP300, FOXA1, HDAC5, HSF4, STAT3, and AR.
statements.note: The abstract lists the eight screened drivers of AR-targeted therapy resistance mutated by APOBEC3B.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Chemotherapy-associated signatures from whole-genome data, together with targeted sequencing of prechemotherapy samples, reconstructed the life-history of 39 therapy-related myeloid malignancies.
statements.evidence: Here, by leveraging distinctive chemotherapy-associated mutational signatures from whole-genome sequencing data and targeted sequencing of prechemotherapy samples, we reconstructed the evolutionary life-history of 39 therapy-related myeloid malignancies.
statements.note: The abstract states the approach and the number of reconstructed malignancies.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients who developed a therapy-related myeloid neoplasm had received more lines of cytotoxic therapy than patients who did not develop one.
statements.evidence: Patients treated with cytotoxic therapies, including autologous stem cell transplantation, are at risk for developing therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (tMN).
statements.note: The abstract names cytotoxic therapy as a risk factor but never compares treatment intensity between patients who did and did not develop tMN.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Neoplasms bearing platinum- and melphalan-induced mutagenesis were hypermutated and enriched for chromothripsis, whereas those with nonmutagenic exposures resembled de novo acute myeloid leukemia.
statements.evidence: neoplasms with evidence of chemotherapy-induced mutagenesis from platinum and melphalan were hypermutated and enriched for complex structural variants (ie, chromothripsis), whereas neoplasms with nonmutagenic chemotherapy exposures were genomically similar to de novo acute myeloid leukemia
statements.note: This dichotomy between mutagenic and nonmutagenic exposures is stated as a result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In myeloma patients given high-dose melphalan with autologous transplantation, tMN could grow from a reinfused clonal hematopoiesis clone that escaped melphalan and was selected after reinfusion.
statements.evidence: For patients with prior multiple myeloma who were treated with high-dose melphalan and autologous stem cell transplantation, we demonstrate that tMN can develop from either a reinfused CH clone that escapes melphalan exposure and is selected after reinfusion
statements.note: The abstract demonstrates this route to tMN in transplanted myeloma patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Circle sequencing of four paired HCC tumor and adjacent nontumor liver samples identified over 230,000 eccDNAs.
statements.evidence: Using the circle-sequencing method, we identify and characterize more than 230,000 eccDNAs from 4 paired samples of HCC tumor and adjacent nontumor liver tissues.
statements.note: The abstract gives both the number of eccDNAs and the number of paired samples.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: eccDNAs were enriched in HCC tumors, arose preferentially from certain chromosomal hotspots, and tracked with differential gene expression.
statements.evidence: EccDNAs are highly enriched in HCC tumors, preferentially originate from certain chromosomal hotspots, and are correlated with differential gene expression.
statements.note: All three properties of the tumor eccDNA profile are reported in that sentence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Outward PCR detected miRNA-17-92-containing eccDNAs in the blood plasma of HCC patients.
statements.evidence: Particularly, a series of eccDNAs carrying the miRNA-17-92 cluster are validated by outward PCR and Sanger sequencing.
statements.note: The abstract reports PCR and Sanger validation of these eccDNAs in tissue and says nothing about plasma or any blood-based assay.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Quantitative PCR showed miRNA-17-92-carrying eccDNAs and their corresponding miRNAs to be elevated in HCC tumors and tied to poor outcomes and patient age.
statements.evidence: Quantitative PCR analyses reveal that miRNA-17-92-containing eccDNAs, along with the expression of their corresponding miRNAs, are elevated in HCC tumors and associated with poor outcomes and the age of HCC patients.
statements.note: The quantitative PCR result and both associations are stated in that sentence.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Templated insertion threads were present in 3% of cancers overall and in as many as 74% of liposarcomas, frequently alongside chromothripsis.
statements.evidence: TI threads occur in 3% of cancers, with a prevalence up to 74% in liposarcoma, and frequent colocalization with chromothripsis.
statements.note: The abstract gives both frequencies and notes the frequent colocalization with chromothripsis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A relevant set of structural variants that drive tumorigenesis escapes discovery when shorter sequencing reads are used.
statements.evidence: Cancer genomes harbor a broad spectrum of structural variants (SVs) driving tumorigenesis, a relevant subset of which escape discovery using short-read sequencing.
statements.note: The abstract states that a relevant subset of tumorigenic structural variants escapes short-read discovery.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Methylome profiling from the long reads uncovered allele-specific methylation, differentially methylated complex rearrangements, and differential promoter methylation in cancer-driver genes.
statements.evidence: We also perform long-read-based methylome profiling and discover allele-specific methylation (ASM) effects, complex rearrangements exhibiting differential methylation, and differential promoter methylation in cancer-driver genes.
statements.note: All three epigenetic findings are listed in that sentence of the abstract.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The post-therapy medulloblastoma carried more templated insertion threads than the diagnostic sample from the same patient.
statements.evidence: We employed Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) long-read sequencing in a paired diagnostic and post-therapy medulloblastoma to unravel the haplotype-resolved somatic genetic and epigenetic landscape.
statements.note: Both time points were sequenced, but the abstract never compares the number of templated insertion threads between them.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Knocking out APOBEC3A cut the SBS2/SBS13 mutation burden of intestinal epithelial organoids.
statements.evidence: The results suggest that the high levels of SBS2/SBS13 in the small intestine are collateral damage from APOBEC1 fulfilling its physiological function of editing APOB mRNA.
statements.note: The abstract attributes these signatures to APOBEC1 activity and reports no knockout and no organoid experiment.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SBS2/SBS13 mutations were present in 17% of the sequenced small-intestinal crypts, a higher frequency than in most other normal tissues.
statements.evidence: Here we whole-genome sequenced 342 microdissected normal epithelial crypts from the small intestines of 39 individuals and found that SBS2/SBS13 mutations were present in 17% of crypts, more frequent than most other normal tissues.
statements.note: The abstract gives the 17% figure and ranks it against most other normal tissues.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Crypts carrying SBS2/SBS13 frequently sat directly beside crypts without these signatures, which points to a cell-intrinsic cause.
statements.evidence: Crypts with SBS2/SBS13 often had immediate crypt neighbors without SBS2/SBS13, suggesting that the underlying cause of SBS2/SBS13 is cell-intrinsic.
statements.note: The neighbouring-crypt observation and the cell-intrinsic reading are both stated in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The small intestine epithelium held very high APOBEC1 mRNA levels, while the large intestine epithelium and other tissues held only low levels.
statements.evidence: APOBEC1 mRNA levels were very high in the small intestine epithelium, but low in the large intestine epithelium and other tissues.
statements.note: The abstract contrasts APOBEC1 mRNA levels between the small intestine epithelium and other tissues.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The mutational processes behind acquired resistance were sought in a clinically annotated set of 3,880 patient samples with tumor-normal sequencing.
statements.evidence: To identify the underlying mutational processes, we utilized a clinically annotated cohort of 3,880 patient samples with tumor-normal sequencing.
statements.note: The abstract states the size and the sequencing design of the cohort used.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: APOBEC3-associated signatures went together with shorter progression-free survival on antiestrogen plus CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy in hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer.
statements.evidence: These signatures correlated with shorter progression-free survival on antiestrogen plus CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy in hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer.
statements.note: The abstract reports this correlation with progression-free survival on that therapy.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Breast tumours with a heavy APOBEC3 signature burden responded better to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
statements.evidence: These studies reveal APOBEC3 mutagenesis to be a frequent mediator of therapy resistance in breast cancer and highlight its potential as a biomarker and target for overcoming resistance.
statements.note: The abstract proposes APOBEC3 as a biomarker and a target but reports no immunotherapy and no response data for it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Signatures of the APOBEC3 enzymes were common across the cohort and enriched in hormone receptor-positive cancers sampled after treatment.
statements.evidence: Mutational signatures associated with apolipoprotein B mRNA-editing enzyme catalytic polypeptide-like 3 (APOBEC3) enzymes were prevalent and enriched in post-treatment hormone receptor-positive cancers.
statements.note: The abstract calls these signatures prevalent and enriched in post-treatment hormone receptor-positive cancers.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Nucleotide excision repair activity governed how unevenly mutation rates ran across the genomes, and transcription-coupled repair reaching past gene boundaries reduced the intergenic mutation rate.
statements.evidence: We find that the activity of NER determines heterogeneity of the mutation rates across skin cancer genomes and that transcription-coupled NER extends beyond the gene boundaries reducing the intergenic mutation rate.
statements.note: Both findings about repair activity and mutation rates are stated in that result sentence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Regular sunscreen use lowers the mutation burden of skin tumours in xeroderma pigmentosum patients.
statements.evidence: Our study unravels the genetic basis of skin cancer risk in XP and provides insights into the mechanisms reducing UV-induced mutagenesis in the general population.
statements.note: The abstract discusses mechanisms that reduce UV-induced mutagenesis but reports nothing about sun protection or any preventive measure.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: For some xeroderma pigmentosum groups the skin cancer risk reaches several thousand-fold that of the general population.
statements.evidence: XP is associated with an increased skin cancer risk, reaching, for some groups, several thousand-fold compared to the general population.
statements.note: The abstract gives this magnitude of skin cancer risk for some XP groups.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Polymerase eta carries out error-free bypass of rare TpG and TpA lesions, of 3' nucleotides in pyrimidine dimers, and of TpT photodimers.
statements.evidence: Mutational profile in XP-V tumors and experiments with POLH knockout cell line reveal the role of polymerase η in the error-free bypass of (i) rare TpG and TpA DNA lesions, (ii) 3' nucleotides in pyrimidine dimers, and (iii) TpT photodimers.
statements.note: The abstract assigns polymerase eta this error-free bypass role based on XP-V tumour profiles and POLH knockout cells.
